title: CISRS remains in CSCS Alliance: scaffolder competence clarity for temporary works

body.p: On 23 November 2026 the Construction Industry Scaffolders Record Scheme (CISRS), a subsidiary of the National Access and Scaffolding Confederation (NASC), confirmed it will remain a member of the CSCS Alliance. The decision follows an agreement to update the Construction Leadership Council (CLC) recommendation on industry card schemes and a new licence agreement with CSCS. CISRS cards will continue to carry the CSCS logo. Clive Dickin, Group CEO of NASC and CISRS, stated that the previous recommendation left CISRS potentially in breach of its licence agreement with CSCS and therefore at risk of termination. The updated CLC wording clarifies that CSCS Alliance schemes may issue cards carrying the CSCS logo to those undertaking recognised construction occupations in any sector or working environment. The arrangement removes the possible need for CISRS cardholders working across different sectors to carry more than one card. Further details of the new licence are expected in the coming days.

Scaffolding is temporary works. Competence of the people who erect, alter, inspect and dismantle scaffolds is a fundamental control under the Work at Height Regulations 2005, CDM 2015 and BS 5975-1:2024. Card schemes such as CISRS provide one recognised route to evidence that competence. Continuity of the CSCS logo on CISRS cards reduces the risk of site-entry or procurement friction for scaffolders working on construction sites and in other sectors. The clarification does not change the duty to plan, supervise and check the scaffold itself. A valid card is not a substitute for a design brief, a Temporary Works Register entry, inspection before use, or a permit-to-load / permit-to-use under the project temporary works procedure.

ul: Treat scaffolding (including proprietary system scaffolds, tube-and-fitting, loading bays and associated ties or kentledge) as temporary works on the Temporary Works Register. Provisional category only — to be confirmed under the project procedure.

Confirm that the scaffold is either built to a design brief and verified design or falls within the scope of a recognised standard solution such as TG20:21, with the relevant compliance sheet completed and available on site.

Require evidence of competence for the persons erecting, altering or dismantling the scaffold. CISRS cards remain one accepted industry route; the project temporary works procedure and the principal contractor still decide what evidence is acceptable.

Ensure the Temporary Works Coordinator or Temporary Works Supervisor controls the sequence: design or compliance check, inspection, permit-to-use, and re-inspection after alteration or adverse weather.
Do not treat a card scheme decision as a change to design responsibility, load capacity or inspection frequency. Those remain project-specific.

Where scaffolders work in non-construction sectors (for example industrial maintenance or energy), confirm that the same temporary works controls apply if the scaffold supports people, plant or materials at height.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Subject to project-specific verification and acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. Exact requirements of BS 5975-1:2024, the Work at Height Regulations 2005, CDM 2015, TG20:21 and any client or principal contractor competence requirements remain those of the appointed designers, the project temporary works procedure and the relevant competent persons. Card schemes support evidence of competence; they do not replace design, inspection or supervision. Further details of the new CISRS–CSCS licence are still to be published. AI-generated or third-party summaries require competent review before use on site.
